title: Hilbert's tenth problem over the rational numbers
main_claim: No algorithm decides whether a polynomial with integer coefficients (any number of variables) has a rational zero. The proof is a Turing reduction from H10 over Z. Each nonconstant f gets an effective sequence of finite rational-solvability tests, and all tests succeed iff f has an integer zero. The converse direction uses compactness, an additive elliptic index map eta into *Z, local formal-log comparisons, and a five-point height bound h(s) <= H*M_S(s)^c.
coverage: Read all of Sections 1-6 of build/sections. Section 2 checked line by line: the local comparison lemma, the theory T and its integer model, Skolemized finite tests and compactness, the coarsening lemma (convex subgroup J, parity of J-values, selection of the branch p_+/p_-, valuation transfer), the index congruences, and the height contradiction including the choice K >= cD and the internal divisibility M^K | delta. Section 3: soundness of Phi checked fully. The Monsky-matrix descent was spot-checked, including the Selmer membership of (beta,1) via K*1_B=0. Use of the companion 2-converse was checked against its Theorem 1.1 statement. Section 4: Shimura curve X_210 genus and quotient, odd-contact ramification lemma, sign-cocycle splitting with order m <= CM, modularity and compatibility, level bound N <= CM^2, isogeny-height chain (Gaudron-Remond applied to J^8 with the Bost lower bound on the complement). The theta/Pazuki base-height lemma was only skimmed. Section 5: verified with sympy that N(d)=7, w=d(1+sqrt2)^3 and w^3-w=-8d (so Q is on E). Also checked the 2-isogeny descent giving rank 1 and the formal-log valuation and tail estimates. Section 6: CRT witness construction (gcd(d1,d2)|4, r not dividing d1*d2), multiplier catalogue, Green-Tao-Ziegler application, Selberg upper sieve, bad-prime count, and fiber sieve. Section 7 not read.

issues.description: Not a gap in this paper, but a load-bearing external dependency. Phi must hold on every integer, which is what makes 'a test failed => no integer zero' sound. That needs a rational point realizing the Selmer class (beta,1) on E_n and E_{n*theta}. With dim Sel_2=3, the case r=0 with a corank-1 divisible part of Sha is excluded only by the companion OpenAI preprint's Theorem 1.1: rational 2-torsion plus 2^infty-Selmer corank <= 1 implies Sha finite. That is a strong, new, unrefereed 2-converse. Its hypotheses are verified correctly here (full rational 2-torsion; corank r+t <= 1 derived from (par:rank-sha)), and the dependence is not circular. The undecidability theorem stands or falls with that companion.
issues.evidence: "The curve has nonzero rational two-torsion, so [PointwiseTwoConverse, Thm 1.1] now applies and proves that Sha(E_l/Q) is finite."

issues.description: Modularity of r_2 is taken from the companion 'Fontaine-Mazur modularity at the prime 2' (no residual hypothesis). This dependency appears avoidable: r_2 comes from a QM building block (A is isogenous to all its Galois conjugates, compatibly with B). Ribet-Pyle theory plus Khare-Wintenberger/Kisin modularity of GL2-type abelian varieties over Q should give the same newform. So this companion is not load-bearing. Noted only as an unverified citation.
issues.evidence: "The modularity input is [OddRegularFontaineMazurAtTwo, Theorem 1.1] in its exact form ... There is no residual-image hypothesis in that statement."

sibling_notes: The family-004 hash had no entries when I read it, so there was no sibling input. The companion preprints (pointwise 2-converse, unrestricted 2-converse/Goldfeld, Fontaine-Mazur at 2) are in the same release. Their audits will decide whether the parity input holds.
